prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1151; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a second vehicle that entered the intersection during the red phase. Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the airbag deployment and impact with the door frame. Police report requested and vehicle photos received from the insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and states they are handling the injury side of the claim directly. Explained the claims process, the documents needed, and the timeline for a bodily injury evaluation. Claimant has not yet received treatment records from the emergency department and will forward them once available.

Entry 3: Reviewed the responding officer's report. Officer documented signal phase observations from two independent witnesses, both consistent with the at-fault vehicle running the red light. Liability appears clear in favor of the insured. Recorded the at-fault driver's insurer and policy details for subrogation.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the claimant showing a closed fracture of the distal radius, treated with immobilization and a follow-up orthopedic appointment scheduled. Claimant reports limited grip strength and missed several days of work. Requested wage documentation and an itemized statement of medical charges.

Entry 5: Followed up with the claimant regarding outstanding documents. Wage verification and the orthopedic follow-up note are still pending. Claimant indicated a preference for direct communication by email. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect the reported injury. File remains open pending receipt of the remaining records and a settlement evaluation.
